copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Croatia v Ghana in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Saturday, and the model and the market disagree on the Croatia side by +15.5pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

Elo numbers going in: Croatia 1860, Ghana 1620. That's a 240-point lead for Croatia — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Croatia to win at 67%, the draw at 16%, and Ghana to win at 17%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Croatia to win at 52%, the draw at 27%, and Ghana to win at 28%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Croatia side — 52% on the market, 67% on the engine, a +15.5pp gap.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Croatia the lower bound is 58%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +6.3pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 39 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Croatia a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +15.5pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: Croatia are favourites on the market at 52% — and the model thinks the market is still underrating them. Our prior reads 67%, a +15.5pp upgrade that crosses the Pick threshold comfortably.
copy.title: Croatia v Ghana · the model leans Croatia
